title: Remove fenced-text tool protocol from supported gameplay providers
description:
Problem
The released gameplay path relied on a custom fenced-text tool-call protocol even though modern model APIs provide native tool/function calling. The provider-neutral Eshyra tool abstraction was the right architecture, but allowing a custom fenced-text default made a model/provider appear supported before its adapter actually implemented native tool transport. This caused eshyra-eznk: Claude Opus could see no native tools and reported that gameplay tools were not actually present.

Decision
A model/provider is not considered supported for released gameplay unless its adapter implements native tool transport for Eshyra's provider-neutral tool definitions. Fenced-text tool calls must not be the default or fallback for any supported gameplay provider.

Scope
- Audit all model providers/adapters and identify any that still use or advertise fenced-text tool calls for gameplay.
- Remove fenced-text as the default gameplay protocol.
- Add explicit provider capability checks: gameplay startup must fail clearly if the selected model adapter cannot transport Eshyra tools natively.
- Update provider/model support docs to distinguish:
  - native-tool supported for gameplay
  - text-only/maintenance-only
  - unsupported until native tool transport is implemented
- Remove prompt instructions that teach supported native providers to emit fenced ```tool_call JSON.
- Keep any fenced parser only if it is explicitly legacy/test-only and unreachable from released gameplay; otherwise delete it.
- Ensure debug logging reports native vs unsupported accurately and never masks unsupported providers behind a fenced fallback.

Acceptance Criteria
- No released gameplay provider defaults to `toolProtocolMode: "fenced-text"`.
- Selecting a provider without native Eshyra tool transport fails before play begins with a clear actionable error.
- Tests cover provider capability enforcement.
- Tests prove supported gameplay providers must forward non-empty native tool definitions when `ModelCompleteInput.tools` is non-empty.
- Prompt snapshots or focused assertions prove native-supported gameplay prompts do not contain fenced tool-call instructions.
- Documentation explains that the core owns provider-neutral tool semantics while adapters own provider-native transport.
- Any remaining fenced-text code is either removed or explicitly marked legacy/test-only with tests proving it is not used by released gameplay.

Dependencies
- Should be started after eshyra-eznk lands, because eznk should establish the first working native AgentSDK/Anthropic gameplay path.
close_reason: Opened PR #249: buildSystemPrompt defaults to native protocol; new assertGameplayCapable startup gate (UnsupportedGameplayProviderError) wired into CLI for primary DM + auditor; fenced parser retained legacy/test-only and unreachable from released gameplay. Tests cover capability enforcement + native-default prompt. ADR 0010 updated. Full verify:worktree green (2093 pass).
